A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
larger AuNPS induce large and amorous Aβ aggregates on the brain lipid-based SLB, whereas, smaller AuNPs promote Aβ protofibril formation.
AuNPs can induce Aβ aggregation on brain SLB and different AuNPs induce different aggregation morphologies.
Aβ aggregation can be modulated by AuNPs of different sizes, shapes and surface charges.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Aβ aggregation can be controlled by the size, charge and shape of the nanoparticles.
different nanostructures can tune Aβ aggregation on brain SLBs, and the resulting Aβ nanostructures have different cytotoxicity.

AuNPs of different shapes and surface charges can induce different Aβ aggregate morphologies and cytotoxicity, which can be useful for developing new strategies to control Aβ aggregation in Alzheimer's disease.
